    Diagnose model convergence and fit

    Source: R/diagnose_model.R
    diagnose_model.Rd

    Checks MCMC convergence diagnostics — R-hat and effective sample size — against user-specified thresholds, and reports any parameters that fail either check. A per-parameter table is also returned, labelling each parameter with the pathogen and time point it refers to, so that convergence problems can be located in time and by pathogen.

    Usage

    diagnose_model(fitted_model, rhat_threshold = 1.1, eff_sample_threshold = 100)

    Arguments

    fitted_model

    A fitted model object of class EpiStrainDynamics.fit, as returned by fit_model().

    rhat_threshold

    R-hat threshold for convergence (default 1.1). Values above this threshold indicate chains have not mixed well.

    eff_sample_threshold

    Effective sample size threshold (default 100). Values below this threshold indicate the posterior samples for a parameter are too autocorrelated to reliably estimate its distribution.

    Value

    An object of class EpiStrainDynamics.diagnostics (a list), returned invisibly, containing:

    convergence

    Logical; TRUE if no parameter fails either threshold

    rhat_issues

    Character vector of parameter names with R-hat above rhat_threshold

    eff_sample_issues

    Character vector of parameter names with effective sample size below eff_sample_threshold

    max_rhat

    The largest R-hat value across all parameters

    min_neff

    The smallest effective sample size across all parameters

    summary

    The full rstan::summary() table the above are derived from

    parameters

    A data frame with one row per parameter and columns parameter (full Stan name), parameter_group (Stan name without indices), pathogen, time_idx (position on the observation-index scale, where 1 is the first observation; fractional for spline coefficients), time (on the time scale of the input data), rhat, n_eff, and the logical flags rhat_issue and eff_sample_issue. See Details.

    rhat_threshold, eff_sample_threshold

    The thresholds the checks used

    Details

    The parameters table identifies each parameter by the exact Stan name before its brackets (parameter_group), and converts the bracketed indices into a pathogen name and a time:

    • log_incidence is the time-varying log-incidence trajectory. Each element is matched to the pathogen and the observation time it belongs to.

    • b_spline_coef, in penalised spline models, holds the spline coefficients. A coefficient does not belong to a single time point, so it is placed at its Greville abscissa (the mean of the interior knots its basis function spans) and converted to the time scale of the data. Coefficients near the edges of the spline can fall before the first or after the last observation. Some of these have no weight on any observation, so only the smoothing prior informs them; a flag on one of them does not mean the fitted trajectory (log_incidence) has failed to converge.

    • noisy_incidence is the pathogen-specific incidence with noise, present when the model includes noise in individual pathogens. It is matched to pathogen and time in the same way as the trajectory.

    • tau is matched to a pathogen when each pathogen has its own smoothing parameter ("independent" smoothing, or a single-pathogen model). With "shared" smoothing one tau applies to all pathogens, so pathogen is NA. With "correlated" smoothing there is no tau; the covariance matrix Sigma is used instead.

    • All other parameters (e.g. phi, eta, Sigma, day_of_week_simplex, lp__) have NA for pathogen and time.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # interactive()
mod <- construct_model(
  pathogen_structure = single(
    data = sarscov2,
    case_timeseries = "cases",
    time = "date"
  ),
  method = random_walk()
)
fit <- fit_model(mod)
diag <- diagnose_model(fit)

# Parameters that failed either check, with pathogen and time attached
diag$parameters[diag$parameters$rhat_issue | diag$parameters$eff_sample_issue, ]
}
